title: Can Catalysis Be Predicted from First Principles?
problem: Investigate the fundamental unresolved challenge of predicting heterogeneous catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability from atomic structure and operating conditions without fitting directly to measured catalyst performance. Use ambient-condition electrochemical nitrogen reduction to ammonia as a stringent case study, including the competing hydrogen evolution reaction and pervasive risk of false-positive ammonia measurements. Evaluate dynamic active sites, reaction pathways, solvent and electrolyte effects, electrochemical potential, uncertainty in electronic-structure approximations, and long-term catalyst reconstruction. Separate established evidence from hypothetical mechanisms, computational predictions, and proposed experiments. Do not assume a viable ambient electrochemical nitrogen-to-ammonia catalyst has been demonstrated by a given study; require rigorous isotope and contamination controls. Seek narrow falsifiable predictions, prospective validation, and explicit failure criteria rather than claiming the general catalytic prediction problem solved.

strategies.title: Active-site identity under operating conditions
strategies.approach: Compare candidate catalytic surface motifs under realistic electrochemical potentials, solvent environments, and adsorbate coverages. Explicitly distinguish idealized pristine surfaces from dynamic active structures and propose in situ tests.
strategies.summary: A ranked set of site hypotheses and falsifiable spectroscopic signatures.

strategies.title: Reaction pathways and selectivity
strategies.approach: Compare associative and dissociative nitrogen reduction pathways against competing hydrogen evolution using uncertainty-aware free-energy profiles. Identify rate-limiting steps and conditions where rankings reverse.
strategies.summary: A microkinetic comparison with a decisive discriminating observable.

strategies.title: Solvent, electrolyte, and potential effects
strategies.approach: Test whether explicit solvent, ionic environment, double-layer effects, and applied potential materially alter predicted barriers and selectivity. Separate approximations from controlled calculations.
strategies.summary: A sensitivity analysis showing which environmental terms change conclusions.

strategies.title: Ammonia contamination and measurement validity
strategies.approach: Design stringent isotope-labeling and blank-control protocols to distinguish genuine N2-derived ammonia from ambient, feedstock, membrane, electrolyte, and laboratory contamination. Include analytical limits and false-positive mechanisms.
strategies.summary: A measurement and controls plan capable of rejecting spurious ammonia production.

strategies.title: Catalyst stability and predictive transfer
strategies.approach: Study catalyst reconstruction, dissolution, poisoning, and long-term activity; design out-of-sample comparisons between predicted and measured catalyst performance. Avoid inferring durability from short simulations or isolated energetics.
strategies.summary: A prospective validation protocol for activity, selectivity, and stability.
